data.gender_notes: Laylah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.

data.etymology: Laylah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Nights.”

in_arabic.name: ليلة
in_arabic.meaning: ليلة تعني الليل الطويل أو ليلة الحبيبة
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم ليلة مشتق من الجذر العربي 'ل ي ل' والذي يعني الليل، ويرتبط بالهدوء والسكينة. في القرآن الكريم، يوصف الليل بالهدوء والراحة. اسم ليلة يعني الليل الطويل أو ليلة الحبيبة، ويحمل دلالات روحية جميلة في الثقافة الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: لیلا
in_urdu.meaning: لیلا مطلب ہے رات یا محبوب کی رات
in_urdu.long_meaning: لیلا نام عربی جڑ 'ل ي ل' سے نکلا ہے جس کا مطلب ہے رات۔ یہ نام رات کی سکون اور امن سے وابستہ ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں میں، یہ نام محبوب یا خاص رات کے معنی میں استعمال ہوتا ہے، جو اسلامی ثقافت میں خوبصورت روحانی معنی رکھتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: लैला
in_hindi.meaning: लैला का अर्थ है रात या प्रेमिका की रात
in_hindi.long_meaning: लैला नाम अरबी मूल 'ल य ल' से आया है, जिसका अर्थ है रात। यह नाम रात की शांति और सुकून से जुड़ा है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम प्रिय या विशेष रात के अर्थ में प्रयोग किया जाता है, जो इस्लामी संस्कृति में सुंदर आध्यात्मिक अर्थ रखता है।

in_pashto.name: لیله
in_pashto.meaning: لیله د شپې یا د محبوبې شپې معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: لیله نوم د عربي ريښې 'ل ي ل' څخه اخیستل شوی دی چې د شپې معنی لري. دا نوم د شپې د آرام او سکون سره تړلی دی. د افغان او پښتن مسلمانانو په دود، دا نوم د محبوبې یا ځانګړې شپې په معنی کارول کیږي، کوم چې په اسلامي کلتور کې ښکلي روحاني معنی لري.

in_english.name: Laylah
in_english.meaning: Laylah means night or beloved's night
in_english.long_meaning: The name Laylah originates from the Arabic root 'ل ي ل' (layl), meaning night. It is associated with tranquility and peace. In Islamic tradition, the name Laylah signifies a long night or a beloved's night, carrying beautiful spiritual connotations. Historically, it has been used across various Muslim cultures, symbolizing serenity and the special bond between loved ones.

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic culture, the term Laylah is associated with various aspects of daily life and religious practices. For instance, in Arabic literature and poetry, Laylah is often used as a romantic or poetic term, evoking the mystery and allure of the night. Additionally, during the month of Ramadan, Muslims observe the nightly Taraweeh Prayers, which are named after Laylah because they take place during the long nights (Laylat al-Qadr, or "Night of Power," which is believed to be the best night of the whole year for Muslims to seek Allah's forgiveness and rewards, usually falls in Laylah).
data.spiritual_significance: In the Islamic context, the spiritual significance of Laylah extends beyond the literal meaning of the word as a measurement of time. It symbolizes tranquility and reflection. Muslims believe that it is during the Laylah that the gates of heaven are open, and during this period, it is believed that worship and supplications are more likely to be accepted by Allah. In the Quran, there are several verses that speak of the night and its spiritual significance. For instance, Surah Al-Inshiriqa (95:1) states, "By the night when it covers (them)." Surah Al-Qaf (50:6-8) speaks of the Day of Judgment, when "no soul will then ask another soul about anything" and "the Messenger conveys what has been revealed to him," alluding to a profound spiritual unity and serenity during the night. Overall, the concept of Laylah in Islamic teachings represents a time of introspection, faith, and closeness to Allah.
